description: The agent must: (1) Read lib/ecommerce/order/processor.ex and the SKILL.md + all referenced markdown files (code-style.md, pattern-matching.md, otp-basics.md, documentation.md). (2) Identify 8 genuine violations: V1=expensive synchronous work in init/1 (must use handle_continue), V2=blocking HTTPClient.get! in handle_call callback (must use Task.async), V3=fire-and-forget notification using GenServer.call instead of cast, V4=with clause in submit_order/1 missing else handler, V5=destructuring payment_info in function body not head in process_refund/1, V6=@moduledoc false on a genuinely public module Ecommerce.Order.Processor, V7=public function submit_order/1 missing @doc and @spec, V8=doctest on side-effectful cancel_order/1 function. (3) Critically NOT flag 3 valid patterns: NV1=single |> pipe in normalize_sku (explicitly valid per skill), NV2=@doc false on handle_call/handle_cast callback implementations (valid per skill), NV3=private validate_order/1 without @spec (private functions exempt per skill). The proprietary traps are: the 'Valid Patterns' section explicitly permits single-pipe chains and @doc false on callbacks — a generic linter would incorrectly flag these; and the context-sensitive rule that @spec is only required for public AND exported functions — private functions must be skipped.
